key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: This combined process offers a promising route to wear-resistant nickel-based protective coatings for mechanical and power engineering components.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel by detonation spraying, then laser remelt.
Compare microstructure, composition and phases using SEM, EDS and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, ball-on-disk wear and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: After remelting, porosity fell from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness rose from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and specific wear rate decreased from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Remelting reduced coating thickness, while corrosion current density improved by only about 3%; wear benefits should not be assumed to imply substantial corrosion protection.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
